key_insight: PARA-PV improves photovoltaic forecasting by combining physics-aware retrieval, a frozen foundation-model prior, and regime-aware distribution shift correction.
engineering_relevance: The method targets more reliable PV power prediction under weather changes, day-night transitions, and critical operating regimes, supporting better grid dispatch and renewable integration.
method: Retrieves historical patches and analog trajectories matched by temporal shape, power level, PV state, and time of day.
Calibrates the retrieved forecast with a frozen Chronos foundation model using a lightweight residual adapter.
Applies physics-aware shift correction and a regime-weighted loss to handle peak, ramping, night-time, and regular conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates evaluation on multivariate PV observations with regime-specific physics constraints and physically grounded correction modules, but it does not report numerical results.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of retrieval matches and the availability of accurate weather, timestamp, and day/night features for shift correction.
paper_title: PARA-PV: Physics-Aware Retrieval-Augmented PV Prediction Based on Frozen Foundation Model and Distribution Shift Correction
